h1: The types of digital marketing, ranked by what they cost you
metaTitle: What Are the Types of Digital Marketing?
metaDescription: The eight types of digital marketing, each with what it costs to run properly in India, how long it takes to work, and the businesses it suits best.
answer: Digital marketing splits into eight channels: search, social, content, email, affiliate, influencer, display and video. They differ mostly in two ways — what they cost to run properly in India, from about ₹15,000 to ₹2,00,000 a month, and how long they take to work, from a week to nine months.
takeaways: Eight channels exist. Most Indian SMBs under ₹50,000/month should run **one**, properly, and ignore the other seven.
The two clocks that matter: **paid channels stop the day you stop paying**, organic channels take months and then keep paying.
Display and affiliate are the two most confidently sold and most consistently wasted line items below ₹5 lakh a month in media.
The cost ranges are wide because the same channel means an intern with Canva at one end and a four-person pod at the other.

sections.h2: The eight channels, with what each one costs in India
body: Every list of digital marketing types you'll find online is roughly the same eight items with different labels. The list isn't the useful part — a definition doesn't help you decide anything. What helps is the price and the clock next to each one.
These are typical Indian market ranges for running the channel properly, meaning with someone competent responsible for it. They exclude your own time, which is not free, and they exclude GST.

rows: Search
Organic search (SEO) plus paid search on Google. Demand capture — people already looking for what you sell.
SEO ₹40,000–₹1,50,000. Ads: media from ₹30,000 plus management ₹25,000–₹75,000 or 10–20% of spend.
Ads: days. SEO: 3–6 months to movement, 12+ to compounding.
Social
Organic posting and community, plus paid social on Meta, Instagram and LinkedIn. Demand creation.
Organic ₹20,000–₹1,00,000. Paid: media from ₹25,000 plus management ₹25,000–₹75,000.
Paid: 2–4 weeks to a readable signal. Organic: 6–9 months.
Content
Articles, guides, comparison pages, video scripts, sales collateral. The fuel every other channel burns.
₹25,000–₹1,00,000 depending on volume. Per article, ₹3,000–₹15,000 for something worth publishing.
3–6 months, and only if it's attached to a distribution channel.
Email
Newsletters, lifecycle flows, abandoned-cart and win-back sequences to a list you own.
₹0–₹15,000 in tooling plus ₹15,000–₹40,000 to actually run it.
Days, if you have a list. Months, if you're building one.
Affiliate
Third parties sending you sales for a cut. Coupon sites, cashback apps, review blogs, comparison portals.
5–20% commission per sale, plus network or platform fees, plus someone to police it.
2–3 months to recruit anyone worth having.
Influencer
Paid or gifted collaborations with creators who already hold your buyer's attention.
Nano creators ₹2,000–₹15,000 per post. Mid-tier ₹50,000–₹3,00,000. Add ₹30,000+ to manage it.
Reach is immediate. Trust and repeat sales are not.
Display
Banner and programmatic ads across networks and apps, bought on impressions. Mostly a reach and retargeting channel.
Media-led. Below ₹1,00,000 a month in spend it rarely clears its own management cost.
Immediate impressions. Direct response is weak outside retargeting.
Video
YouTube, Reels, Shorts — organic and paid. The most expensive to produce, the hardest to fake.
₹15,000–₹2,00,000 per asset depending on production. Paid distribution on top.
Weeks for paid. 6–12 months for an organic channel to compound.

sections.h2: Two of these are really four
body: Search and social each hide a split that changes everything about how they behave, and lists that treat them as single channels mislead people into budgeting badly.

**Search** is organic and paid. Same intent, opposite economics. Paid search bills you per click forever and stops dead the day the card fails. Organic search costs more up front, takes months, and then keeps delivering after you stop spending — which is exactly why its cost per lead falls over time while paid's rises with competition. If you want the fuller version, we've written about [where SEO fits inside digital marketing](/answers/what-is-seo-in-digital-marketing).

**Social** is organic and paid, and they're barely the same discipline. Organic social builds an audience slowly and cheaply and is largely unmeasurable at the lead level. Paid social buys attention instantly, measurably, and only for as long as you pay. Agencies that quote you "social media marketing" as one number are usually selling you the organic half and quietly billing management on the paid half.
Count them properly and you have ten things to fund, not eight. Which is the whole argument for funding one.

callout.title: The proposal tell
callout.body: If a proposal lists a channel without separating media spend from management fee, you can't tell what you're paying for work versus what's going to Google or Meta. Ask for it split. Our performance retainers bill spend separately with zero media markup, precisely so that line stays legible.

body: The honest version of channel selection isn't a matrix. It's one question: where does your buyer already go when they have this problem? Everything else is a rationalisation.
Some patterns hold reliably in the Indian market:
bullets: **B2B and SaaS** — search first, almost always. Long consideration cycles, buyers who research, low volume but high value per lead. LinkedIn paid second, if your deal size is above roughly ₹2 lakh. Email third. Ignore display entirely.

**D2C and ecommerce** — paid social and marketplaces first, because discovery happens on a feed. Search second, once you know which products convert. Influencer fourth, and only with creators whose audience actually buys.

**Local services** — Google Business Profile, reviews and local search, and then stop. A dentist in Indiranagar does not need a content calendar. Paid search on a tight radius is the only ad channel worth funding.
**High-ticket services** — content and search, plus the founder being visible on LinkedIn. Nobody spends ₹15 lakh because of a banner ad.
**Consumer apps** — paid social and app store optimisation, with video as the creative engine. Search matters far less than the store listing.
**Anything with a genuinely new category** — social, video and PR, because nobody is searching for a thing they don't know exists. SEO cannot capture demand that hasn't formed yet.

sections.h2: The channels most Indian SMBs should skip
body: This is the part that gets cut from most articles on this topic, because listing eight channels and recommending all eight is how agencies sell eight retainers.
Below roughly ₹1,00,000 a month in total marketing budget, three of the eight are actively bad bets:
numbered: **Display.** Programmatic banner buying has a fixed cost of competence — someone has to build audiences, exclude junk placements and read the reports. Below about ₹1,00,000 a month in media, that cost eats the return. The exception is straightforward retargeting of your own site visitors, which is cheap and works.

**Affiliate.** Recruiting, tracking and policing affiliates is a job. Run it badly and you pay commission on sales you'd have made anyway, mostly to coupon extensions that intercept the last click. Worth it above real volume, wasteful below it.

**Mid-tier influencer.** The ₹50,000-to-₹3,00,000 creator tier is where the most money disappears with the least evidence. Follower counts are purchasable, engagement is gameable, and one post is not a campaign. Nano creators at ₹2,000–₹15,000, in volume, with a tracked code, is a defensible test. One big name is a donation.

callout.title: Skip isn't never
callout.body: All three of these work at scale. The question isn't whether the channel is real — it's whether your budget clears the fixed cost of running it competently. Most don't, and being told so before you spend is cheaper than finding out after.

sections.h2: Why the ranges are so wide
body: A ₹25,000 SEO retainer and a ₹1,50,000 SEO retainer are both called SEO. They are not the same product, and the difference isn't margin.
Four things move the number, and they move it a lot:
bullets: **Who does the work.** A junior executive running five accounts costs a fraction of a specialist running two. You can see this in the output within a month.
**Whether production is included.** Content, creative and video are the expensive bits. Some quotes include them, most don't, and that single line explains most price gaps between proposals.
**Competition in your category.** Ranking a plumber in Nagpur and ranking a fintech nationally are different orders of difficulty at every stage.
**Whether media spend is bundled.** A ₹1,00,000 quote that includes ₹60,000 of ad spend is a ₹40,000 service. Read the split before comparing anything.

body: The most common failure we see isn't picking the wrong channel. It's picking six, funding each at a quarter of what it needs, and concluding after a year that digital marketing doesn't work. It worked fine. It was never switched on.

A workable rule: fund one channel to the level where it can genuinely perform, run it for 90 days, and only add a second when the first is producing leads you can trace. There's a full protocol in [how to do digital marketing on a small budget](/answers/how-to-do-digital-marketing), and the individual line items are priced out in [what digital marketing services cost](/answers/what-are-digital-marketing-services).

For what it's worth, we sell three of the eight — SEO from ₹75,000/mo, organic social and content at ₹30,000/₹50,000/₹70,000, and performance marketing at ₹40,000/₹75,000/₹1,50,000. We don't sell display, affiliate or influencer management, because we're not good enough at them to guarantee anything, and the guarantee is the whole product.

faqs.q: How many types of digital marketing are there?
faqs.a: Eight, if you count sensibly: search, social, content, email, affiliate, influencer, display and video. Some lists inflate this to fifteen by splitting SEO into three and calling mobile and WhatsApp separate channels. They aren't channels, they're surfaces the same eight run on.

faqs.q: Which type of digital marketing is best for a small business in India?
faqs.a: Whichever one your buyers already use. For local services it's Google Business Profile and local search. For D2C it's paid social. For B2B it's search plus email. The worst answer is all of them at a quarter of the required budget each.

faqs.q: What's the cheapest digital marketing channel to start with?
faqs.a: Email, if you already have a list — the tooling has genuinely usable free tiers and the audience is yours rather than rented. If you have no list, paid search is the cheapest way to test whether anyone wants what you sell, because ₹25,000 buys a readable answer in a fortnight.

faqs.q: How long does each digital marketing channel take to work?
faqs.a: Paid search and paid social give a readable signal in days to weeks. Email is immediate with an existing list. SEO, content and organic social take three to nine months. Anyone compressing the organic timelines is describing a smaller, easier problem than the one you have.

faqs.q: Do I need an agency for all eight channels?
faqs.a: No, and an agency offering all eight at a small budget is usually one team doing all eight thinly. Pick the two that match where your buyers are, and hire depth in those. Breadth costs the same and delivers a fraction of the result.
